newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-FRANCE MEET BRAZIL IN WORLD CUP DRESS REHEARSAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FRANCE MEET BRAZIL IN WORLD CUP DRESS REHEARSAL.

text.p: France open their Tournoi de France World Cup dress rehearsal against world champions Brazil on Tuesday in what home fans see as the ideal final to next year's tournament proper.

The match, first of six in the nine-day event also involving England and Italy, has taken on added meaning after Brazil's shock 4-2 defeat by Norway in Oslo on Friday which ended the debate as to how long they had been unbeaten.
"We don't usually repeat two bad games in a row. Even if we don't show it our pride is hurt. And all will return to normal in front of the French," said Brazil defender Aldair.

France coach Aime Jacquet's objective is for France to win their three matches and progress in their search for the attack they need if they are to claim at last the World Cup Frenchman Jules Rimet created nearly 70 years ago.

Jacquet has refused to even hint at his line-up because of the short period of time he has with the whole squad before the match. Six players still involved in Italian league action did not join the squad until Sunday night.

The delay, which annoyed Jacquet, has prevented him from his stated intent of trying new attacking combinations against Brazil but he hopes the tournament as a whole will help his side become more versatile.

He does, however, have the encouraging experience of a win over the Netherlands in February when, after France had fallen behind, he made a substitution after 30 minutes that altered the composition of the side and the complexion of the match.

Brazil's vastly experienced coach Mario Zagallo will be aware of the growing tactical nous of his immediate adversary as he prepares his team for a victory they need to reassert their status as the world's best side and favourites to retain their title next year.
He will have noted how Norway, in the words of their coach Egil Olsen, won by "denying them space, breaking down their midfield-attack link and so their lines of provision to Ronaldo and Romario."
Zagallo is planning two changes from the side that lost to Norway, with Roma's Aldair replacing his 1994 World Cup partner Marcio Santos at the back and Giovanni coming in for Djalminha in midfield.
"This is just an adjustment. It doesn't mean I've put a cross against Marcio Sanos and Djalminha," he said.

Giovanni, who with Djalminha was preferred to Juninho in the Brazil squad for the Tournoi and Copa America, may be regarded as able to link better with his Barcelona team mate Ronaldo, who was very quiet in Oslo where he was probably unable to shake off the worries of his much-discussed club future.

The Brazilians expressed considerable surprise at the standard of the Norwegian team and may have come to Europe with a false sense of security following a 4-0 thrashing of Mexico in a recent friendly in Miami.
Brazil will be looking for their fifth victory over France in their eighth meeting since the 1958 World Cup semifinals.

Two players, Laurent Blanc and Didier Deschamps, remain in the probable French side from the last meeting, a 2-0 victory for Brazil in Paris in 1992. The Brazilian survivors are goalkeeper Taffarel, midfielder Mauro Silva and Romario.

Michel Platini, joint president of the World Cup organising committee, will recall as he watches the match his goal in France's only outright win over Brazil, 1-0 in Paris in 1981. He was captain of the side that won their epic 1986 World Cup quarter-final on penalties.
France - Fabien Barthez; Lilian Thuram, Laurent Blanc, Marcel Desailly, Bixente Lizarazu; Ibrahim Ba, Christian Karembeu, Didier Deschamps, Zinedine Zidane; Patrice Loko, Robert Pires.
Brazil - Taffarel; Cafu, Aldair, Celio Silva, Roberto Carlos; Mauro Silva, Dunga, Giovanni, Leonardo; Ronaldo, Romario.
